title: Machine Learning Aboard the ADAPT Gamma-Ray Telescope
problem: Real-time detection and localization of short-duration gamma-ray bursts requires neural networks that operate under severe size, weight, and power constraints aboard an orbital telescope, replacing resource-intensive ground-based computations.
motivation: On-board GRB detection and localization enables real-time multi-messenger observations of transient phenomena in deep space.
method: A neural network pipeline consisting of two specialized networks performs on-board GRB analysis: one filters background radiation for signal discrimination, while the second estimates directional uncertainty for individual gamma-ray photons. Networks are trained and validated using physical GRB detection simulations from ADAPT, a high-altitude balloon-borne prototype telescope.
key_novelty: Deployment of compact neural networks for real-time on-board gamma-ray burst localization on resource-constrained space platforms.
contributions: Neural network pipeline for on-board GRB localization under strict SWaP (size, weight, power) constraints
Background radiation filtering network for accurate signal discrimination
Uncertainty estimation network for gamma-ray photon source direction constraints
Validation framework using ADAPT prototype with physical GRB detection simulations
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: On-board neural network inference for space-based astrophysics
